function.name: write_app
function.description: Create an interactive React app (dashboard, explorer) and open it on the canvas: a new file (filename), or a full rewrite of an existing app (path + expected_content_hash), saved in place. It runs in a sandbox without network access and reads the declared workspace tables live through @df/data hooks. For small changes to an existing app, use edit_file replacements instead.

plan_step.description: When working through a checklist plan: the number (1-based) of the plan step this result serves. Several results can serve one step; a step is checked off once you move on to a later step or finish.

replaces.description: The app's files/... path, equal to path. Only to fix an app the user says is wrong, broken, or unwanted (or one this run made that turned out wrong): the fixed app moves to after the latest request and the thread notes that it replaced the old one. Omit it for ordinary changes the user asks for.

filename.description: For a new app: a visible filename ending in .app.jsx, without directories, for example sales_explorer.app.jsx.

path.description: To rewrite an existing agent-editable app in place: its files/... path (ending in .app.jsx). Omit filename when you pass path.

expected_content_hash.description: With path: the app's current content_hash. On conflict, reread the app before retrying.

title.description: Short single-line title shown to the user (at most 80 characters).

tables.description: Workspace table names the app reads with @df/data hooks. Only these tables are available to the app.

sources.description: Connected sources the app queries live with useSourceQuery from @df/data: reference ids of external sources in this session (add one with propose_data_operation). Live queries read the source each time the app runs; prefer declared workspace tables for data already loaded.

code.description: The complete single-file React app: imports only from react, @df/ui, @df/data, @df/chart, @df/format, @df/icons, @mui/material, d3, lodash, or @df/geo, and `export default function App()`.

function.name: write_html_app
function.description: Create an interactive HTML app and open it on the canvas: a new file (filename), or a full rewrite of an existing app (path + expected_content_hash), saved in place. The app runs in a sandbox without network access and reads the declared workspace tables live through the DF runtime. For small changes to an existing app, use edit_file replacements instead.

plan_step.description: When working through a checklist plan: the number (1-based) of the plan step this result serves. Several results can serve one step; a step is checked off once you move on to a later step or finish.

replaces.description: The app's files/... path, equal to path. Only to fix an app the user says is wrong, broken, or unwanted (or one this run made that turned out wrong): the fixed app moves to after the latest request and the thread notes that it replaced the old one. Omit it for ordinary changes the user asks for.

filename.description: For a new app: a visible filename ending in .html, without directories, for example sales_explorer.html.

path.description: To rewrite an existing agent-editable app in place: its files/... path (ending in .html). Omit filename when you pass path.

expected_content_hash.description: With path: the app's current content_hash. On conflict, reread the app before retrying.

title.description: Short single-line title shown to the user (at most 80 characters).

tables.description: Workspace table names the app reads with DF.query or DF.table. Only these tables are available to the app.

sources.description: Connected sources the app queries live with DF.sourceQuery: reference ids of external sources in this session (add one with propose_data_operation). Live queries read the source each time the app runs; prefer declared workspace tables for data already loaded.

html.description: The complete HTML document, with inline CSS and JavaScript only. Do not load external scripts, stylesheets, fonts, or images.
